chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The believer is not shy/embarrassed from his brother, and it is not known which of the two is more wonderful: the one who burdens his brother to make effort for him when he enters, or the one who is burdened by his brother.

key_terms.أَخِيهِ: his brother (referring to a fellow believer)
key_terms.يَحْتَشِمُ: to be shy or modest (in a positive sense of not hesitating to ask)

ai.seo_question: What does the concept of 'not being shy' (la yaktashimu) mean in the context of brotherhood between believers?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the believer's character through the removal of 'ihtisham' (excessive shyness or reserve) in social interactions, fostering a culture of mutual service. It illustrates the ideal of 'takaful' (solidarity) where the distinction between giver and receiver blurs, as both are equally rewarded for their sincerity. This reflects the Shia emphasis on deep, practical brotherhood that extends beyond ritual piety into daily domestic life.
